Definition: Echud, the name of three Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Ehud is the name of three Israelites in the records, and this single verse names one of them, a Benjamite listed among the sons of Ehud's line in the days of the return. The better-known Ehud is the left-handed judge who killed Eglon of Moab, but the man in this verse is only a name in a genealogy. The lists keep him because the family line mattered, even when the story does not.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that God remembers names the story forgets, and every one of them belonged to a real person in a real family. The genealogy is not filler; it is His record.
